REFERRAL COVER SHEET

Referral Number: FDNS-DNZ-26-04321
Referring Office: USCIS FDNS, Fraud Detection and National Security Directorate, Fresno Field Office
Date: 2026-09-30

Subject: Rajesh Kumar (A091-456-123) – Previously known as Vikram Singh (A076-789-456)

Basis: Identity fraud, prior removal, and unlawful re-entry; subject to revocation of naturalization under 8 U.S.C. 1451(a) for procuring naturalization illegally by concealing material facts.

Summary of Derogatory Information: A fingerprint records digitization review under the Operation Janus successor initiative matched a latent print from the subject's current A-file to an alien registration file under the identity 'Vikram Singh' (DOB: 1971-08-25). The Singh file indicates an IN ABSENTIA ORDER OF REMOVAL issued administratively on 1999-11-03 by the former Immigration and Naturalization Service. The subject, as Singh, was fingerprinted at the time of the removal proceeding. The subject subsequently re-entered the United States without inspection, applied for asylum under the name Kumar, and was granted asylum (I-589 approved 2001-03-22) and LPR status (I-485 approved 2004-07-19). Subject naturalized as a U.S. citizen on 2009-06-15, based on his LPR status. The N-400 application filed under the Kumar identity made no reference to the prior removal order, the different name, or the prior immigration history. This concealment is material to the naturalization decision. The subject currently owns and operates a trucking fleet in Fresno, CA. No prior criminal history noted.

REFERRAL COVER SHEET

Referral Number: FDNS-DNZ-26-04456
Referring Office: USCIS FDNS, Fraud Detection and National Security Directorate, Houston Field Office
Date: 2026-10-02

Basis: Criminal conduct during statutory period and prior to oath; material misrepresentation on naturalization application. Subject to revocation under 8 U.S.C. 1451(a).

Summary of Derogatory Information: Subject, Chinwe Okafor, naturalized as a U.S. citizen on 2017-05-19. On 2022-04-12, subject was convicted in the United States District Court for the Southern District of Texas (Case #4:21-CR-00891) of one count of conspiracy to commit health care fraud, in violation of 18 U.S.C. 1349 and 1347. The conviction stems from a scheme involving fraudulent Medicare billing for home health services that were not provided. The indictment and evidence established that the fraudulent billing activity occurred between January 2014 and December 2018, which includes the period within five years immediately preceding the naturalization application and before the date of the oath of allegiance. Subject was sentenced to 48 months imprisonment and ordered to pay $3,100,000 in restitution. In her N-400 application, filed 2016-08-20, subject answered 'No' to the question: 'Have you EVER committed, assisted in committing, or attempted to commit, a crime or offense for which you were NOT arrested?' This answer was false; the subject's participation in the fraudulent scheme was ongoing at the time of the application. The crime was a violation of 8 U.S.C. 1101(f)(3) and constituted a lack of good moral character. Subject is the owner of a home-health agency in Houston, TX.

REFERRAL COVER SHEET

Referral Number: ICE-HRVWC-26-00123
Referring Office: ICE HSI Human Rights Violators and War Crimes Center (HRVWCC), Washington, DC
Date: 2026-10-10

Basis: Participation in extrajudicial killing and persecution; lack of good moral character; fraud or misrepresentation in naturalization proceedings. Subject to revocation under 8 U.S.C. 1451(a).

Summary of Derogatory Information: Subject, Rigoberto de la Cruz, a former member of the Guatemalan Army's Special Forces (Kaibil) unit, is implicated in the December 1982 village massacre in Peten, Guatemala. Declassified State Department and CIA records, as well as witness testimony given in Guatemalan judicial proceedings (Caso Ixil), state that subject was present and participated in the killing of unarmed civilians. Subject entered the United States in 1985 without inspection. He was granted LPR status under INA 245(A) in July 1996 (based on IRCA). He filed for naturalization on 2007-01-15 and took the oath on 2008-08-21. In his N-400, he answered 'No' to questions regarding prior military service and to engaging in any activity related to genocide, torture, or killing. These answers were false and concealed material facts regarding his military background and involvement in human rights violations. The subject is currently a landscaping business owner in Palm Beach County, FL. He has no known criminal record in the U.S. His participation in the massacre makes him ineligible for naturalization under INA 316 and removable for having assisted in persecution.

Referring Office: USCIS Chicago Field Office, FDNS Unit
Date: 2026-09-18
Basis: 8 U.S.C. 1451 — Illegal procurement (marriage fraud), no bona fide marriage at time of naturalization.
Summary: Subject naturalized as LPR through marriage to a U.S. citizen (filed I-130/I-485 in 2007; approved 2008). On 2024-03-12, ICE HSI Chicago interviewed the former spouse, who recanted the marriage, stating she was paid $15,000 to petition for the subject and never cohabitated with him. She provided a sworn statement and produced copies of cash withdrawals correlating with the payment. Bank records subpoenaed in 2026 show a series of $5,000 withdrawals from the subject's account in the months preceding the I-130 filing, matching the ex-wife's account deposits. The subject's N-400 (filed 2012) and naturalization interview affirmatively asserted a bona fide marital union. FDNS recommends revocation referral to DOJ.
